analysis.summary: The claude-core-skills library has zero prior art on cross-vendor delegation: no consideration, test, or record of Codex, GPT, or any non-Anthropic model as implementer or reviewer anywhere in skills, hooks, instructions, evals, or experiments — the only Codex/OpenAI mentions are descriptions of third-party repos' agent-CLI compatibility inside the 2026-07-13 external-skill-analysis. What it does have is substantial Anthropic-internal multi-MODEL infrastructure: Opus-vs-Sonnet headless A/B machinery (fresh `claude -p` runs with `--model` pinned, lockfile-guarded arm toggling of ~/.claude/skills, FIRED measured as observed Skill-tool invocations in stream-json transcripts, blind grading, pre-registration by commit hash) plus a reusable cross-model path-consistency instrument in evals/ with a completed Sonnet-vs-Opus run in results/2026-07-15/. Conventions are firm: dated artifacts live at `results/<date>/` (topic subdirectory for distinct investigations), accepted evidence requires a pre-registered experiments/hypothesis-*.md, N=2 fresh-session A/B, verbatim transcripts, dated rates never promoted to "always," and any-regression-blocks; failures become DEAD-n entries in .claude/LESSONS.md. Hooks and instructions delegate nothing externally — the sole hook is a bash+jq context-injection reminder and the instructions file steers Claude's own governors. On adopting third-party skills, the 2026-07-13 report is the controlling precedent: adversarial refutation downgraded 10 of 13 high-tier calls, nothing new earns always-on, external ideas fold into core skills only through research-methodology gates, and licensing/trust flags plus register-then-verify install discipline apply to anything brought in.
